title: Punctual purity of monomial hypersurfaces over a trait
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal; a uniformizer $\pi$ is a generator of that maximal ideal.

Let $\ell$ be invertible in $R$, fix a uniformizer $\pi$, let $n\geq1$, and let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be nonnegative integers not all zero. Then the Noetherian scheme
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(T_1^{e_1}\cdots T_n^{e_n}-\pi)\bigr)$$
is regular and punctually pure. The assertion allows zero exponents and exponents divisible by $\ell$ or by the positive residue characteristic; no completeness, henselianity, or excellence of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definition 3.5.11 and Proposition 3.5.12 with proof and Lemma 3.5.13(i)--(vi), printed pp.250--251; section 3.5 begins on printed p.248 with an arbitrary trait.

proof.text:
Write $V_R(a)=\operatorname{Spec}R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(\prod T_i^{a_i}-\pi)$. The trait ring is a DVR by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. For any $d\geq1$, apply [lem-sfb-eisenstein-quotient-dvr] to $Z^d-\pi$: its constant coefficient is in $(\pi)\setminus(\pi^2)$ (otherwise cancellation would make $\pi$ a unit), and its other lower coefficients are zero. Thus $R_d=R[z]/(z^d-\pi)$ is a DVR with uniformizer $z$, and [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] makes $\operatorname{Spec}R_d$ a trait. The image of the inverse of $\ell$ remains an inverse. There is an explicit ring isomorphism
$$R_d[T]/(\prod T_i^{a_i}-z)\simeq R[T]/((\prod T_i^{a_i})^d-\pi):$$
it fixes each $T_i$, sends $z$ to $\prod T_i^{a_i}$, and its inverse sends each $T_i$ to its class. The two relations verify both composites. Hence $V_{R_d}(a)\simeq V_R(da)$ as schemes. Punctual purity is preserved by this isomorphism: the local rings, residue fields and dimensions identify, and [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] identifies the Kummer maps under isomorphism base change.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(ii) and footnote viii, printed p.251; auxiliary algebra also Stacks Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, final sentence of proof, and Tag 00PD.

proof.text: First prove regularity and integrality for every nonzero exponent vector, independently of purity. In fraction-field characteristic zero some positive exponent is invertible, so apply [lem-per-primitive-monomial-trait-geometry]. In characteristic $p>0$, let $r$ be the minimum $p$-adic valuation of the positive exponents and write $e_i=p^r a_i$ (zero entries stay zero). Some $a_i$ is prime to $p$, hence invertible in the fraction field of the root trait $R_{p^r}$ from Step 1, which still has characteristic $p$. Apply the same primitive geometry statement to $V_{R_{p^r}}(a)$ and use the explicit isomorphism of Step 1. This proves that every $V_R(e)$ under consideration is a Noetherian regular integral scheme, without any excellence or separability assumption.

For the all-one vector, [lem-per-semistable-coordinate-divisor-purity] gives the supported Kummer isomorphism for each coordinate divisor. Step 2 supplies regularity, so [lem-per-monomial-boundary-purity-criterion] gives punctual purity of $V_R(1,\ldots,1)$. This holds over every auxiliary trait as well. Applying it over $R_d$ and using Step 1 gives punctual purity of $V_R(d,\ldots,d)$ for every $d\geq1$. This is an isomorphism of underlying schemes, so no descent along the possibly inseparable root-trait morphism is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.12 proof, all-one case and auxiliary trait, with Lemma 3.5.13(ii),(iv), printed p.251.

proof.text: Now suppose every $a_i>0$ and $\ell\nmid a_i$. Put $d=\operatorname{lcm}_i a_i$ and $b_i=d/a_i$. The map $Y=V_R(d,\ldots,d)\to X=V_R(a)$ sends $T_i$ to $U_i^{b_i}$. Its algebra is $\mathcal O(X)[U_1,\ldots,U_n]/(U_i^{b_i}-T_i)_i$: eliminating the $T_i$ leaves precisely $\prod U_i^d-\pi$. Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] gives the basis $\prod U_i^{c_i}$ with $0\leq c_i<b_i$, hence constant positive rank $\prod b_i$, prime to $\ell$. Both schemes are regular by Step 2. For $H_i=V(T_i)$ the reduced inverse image is $H'_i=V(U_i)$, since the inverse image is cut out by $U_i^{b_i}$ and $\mathcal O(Y)/(U_i)=\kappa(s)[U_j:j\ne i]$. These are the regular effective Cartier divisors in [lem-per-monomial-boundary-purity-criterion]. By Step 3 and that criterion all pairs $(Y,H'_i)$ are pure. Apply [lem-per-finite-flat-regular-divisor-purity-descent] to each pair, then the criterion on $X$. Thus $V_R(a)$ is punctually pure. This uses no generic-etaleness hypothesis.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(v) and its proof, using Proposition 3.4.3, printed pp.246,251.

proof.text: For positive $e_i$, induct on $N=\sum_i v_\ell(e_i)$. The base $N=0$ is Step 4. If $N>0$, choose $j$ with $\ell\mid e_j$ and put $a_j=e_j/\ell$, $a_i=e_i$ otherwise. The induction hypothesis gives punctual purity of $X=V_R(a)$. Set $D=V(T_j)$; the boundary criterion gives purity of $(X,D)$ and says that $D$ is regular effective Cartier. Conditions (a) and (c) of [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] therefore give punctual purity of $D$. Apply [lem-per-kummer-root-regular-divisor-purity] to the nonzerodivisor $T_j$ in the regular affine scheme $X$. Eliminating $T_j$ identifies its root algebra with $X'=V_R(e)$, and $D'=V(U)\simeq D$. The cited root statement gives regularity of $X'$, purity of $(X',D')$, and an etale map $X'\setminus D'\to X\setminus D$. Conditions (a) and (b) of two-of-three give punctual purity of $X'$ at every point of $D'$. On the complement, [lem-per-punctual-purity-etale-locality] gives purity from that of $X$; open restriction has the same local rings and Kummer maps. Thus every point of $X'$ is pure. This completes the induction; it does not assume that purity of just one boundary pair implies purity everywhere.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.13(vi), printed p.251; Proposition 3.4.5, printed pp.246--248; Proposition 3.2.3, printed p.244, spells out the boundary/complement inference.

proof.text: Finally let $I=\{i:e_i>0\}$, which is nonempty, and let $m$ be the number of zero exponents. Reordering variables gives the literal polynomial-ring identification $V_R(e)\simeq\mathbf A^m_{V_R((e_i)_{i\in I})}$. The positive-exponent base is regular and punctually pure by Steps 2 and 5 and is of finite type over the original trait. Its affine-space projection is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], is of finite type by its finite polynomial presentation, and has Noetherian source by Step 2. Therefore [lem-per-smooth-punctual-purity-ascent] proves regularity and punctual purity of $V_R(e)$. This includes $m=0$ and proves the entire statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.12 proof, zero-exponent reduction using Corollary 3.5.6, printed pp.249,251.

split_report.summary: Reconstructed the ILO XVI assembly using the six re-admitted UNSPLIT source interfaces, with an explicit root-trait substitution, characteristic-power regularity reduction, monic power-map basis and prime-to-ell descent, induction on ell-valuations using two-of-three and etale locality on the complement, and smooth ascent for zero exponents. No new nodes or theorem attachments; statement, source, stmt_deps, searches and blueprint provenance preserved.
split_report.blueprint: Retains the historical ancestor/via provenance of the regular finite-coefficient input, specifically the ILO XVI Theorem 3.6.2 final reduction to Proposition 3.5.12 recorded in blueprint.from.place. Realizes Proposition 3.5.12 by Lemma 3.5.13(i)--(vi). The current latest ancestor text is provenance only: this split does not invoke the discarded Artin-Gabber proof or arbitrary-field adic duality.

tool_uses.why: Generic algebra supplies the auxiliary root trait for the explicit source ring substitution; no purity or perverse statement is imported.
Generic smoothness of a finite affine-space projection verifies the hypothesis of the unit-local smooth punctual-purity ascent input.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q91-2931226bf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read ILO XVI 3.5.11, 3.5.12 and 3.5.13(i)-(vi) with fn viii (pp.250-251) and every cited statement; the item statement matches 3.5.12 and is unchanged. Without new nodes, the six steps realize (iii), (ii), the all-one case, (v), (vi) and the 3.5.6 zero-exponent reduction. The six source interfaces are unsplit on this base, so the NR 79925f64 obstruction is gone; no cycle (BFS). Steps checked: Step 1, Eisenstein Z^d-pi and the explicit iso V_{R_d}(a)=V_R(da). Step 2, the char-p reduction e=p^r a feeding primitive geometry. Step 4, rank prod(d/a_i) prime to ell and reduced pullback V(U_i). Step 5, induction on sum v_ell, two-of-three (a)+(c) then (a)+(b), and etale locality on the complement. Step 6, A^m over the base and smooth ascent. Edge cases checked: e=1, e=ell, zero exponents, p-divisible exponents, (2,3). Batch-5 flag: two-of-three and etale-locality reach sec-trace-formula only via class-calculus -> regular-flag-blowup -> def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra. That is a general symmetric-algebra definition, not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality, and class-calculus is already a stmt_dep of the item, so the citations are outside the assumptions. Accepted tool_uses: lem-sfb-eisenstein-quotient-dvr and sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth; the worker wrote tool_uses themselves (C8), but the content is acceptable. No changes.
